sentences.en: Many Americans feel they are embattled in a culture war that is not only dividing them, but stressing them out.
sentences.zh: 许多美国人觉得他们卷入了一场文化战争，这不仅在撕裂他们，还给他们带来了巨大的精神压力。

sentences.en: An American Psychological Association survey showed that 52% of American adults report that the 2016 election is a significant source of stress.
sentences.zh: 美国心理学协会的一项调查显示，52%的美国成年人表示2016年大选是他们压力的一个重要来源。

sentences.en: This type of stress could be largely related to people's differing views on what is fact and what is moral.
sentences.zh: 这种压力在很大程度上可能与人们对什么是事实、什么是道德持有不同观点有关。

sentences.en: In this episode,
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，

sentences.en: we speak with a psychologist about how scientific research into how people think and behave can help us understand how we became so divided and how we can come back together.
sentences.zh: 我们邀请了一位心理学家，探讨如何通过对人类思维和行为的科学研究，来理解我们为何会产生如此深刻的分歧，以及我们如何才能重新走到一起。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton, and this is Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿，这里是《心理学话语》。

sentences.en: Jonathan Haidt is a social psychologist at New York University's Stern School of Business.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·海特是纽约大学斯特恩商学院的一位社会心理学家。

sentences.en: His research has focused on the moral foundations of politics and on ways to transcend the culture wars by using recent discoveries in moral psychology to foster more civil forms of politics.
sentences.zh: 他的研究重点是政治的道德基础，以及如何利用道德心理学的最新发现来超越文化战争，从而促进更具文明素养的政治形式。

sentences.en: He is the author of The Happiness Hypothesis and of the New York Times bestseller The Righteous Mind, Why Good People Are Divided by Politics and Religion.
sentences.zh: 他是《幸福假说》以及《纽约时报》畅销书《正义之心：为什么好人总是因政治和宗教而分歧》的作者。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Haidt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，海特博士。

sentences.en: Thank you, Audrey.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，奥黛丽。

sentences.en: Pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: So, civility in politics, that sounds like a pipe dream, especially in a presidential election year.
sentences.zh: 那么，政治中的文明素养，听起来像是一个不切实际的幻想，尤其是在一个总统大选年。

sentences.en: What do you mean by a civil form of politics?
sentences.zh: 你所说的文明形式的政治是指什么？

sentences.en: People are very good at relating to each other in different ways.
sentences.zh: 人们非常擅长以各种不同的方式与彼此相处。

sentences.en: We're extremely good at adversarial forms, at attacking each other, at being lawyers, at fighting.
sentences.zh: 我们极擅长对抗性的形式，擅长攻击彼此，擅长像律师一样辩论，擅长争斗。

sentences.en: And we're also really good at cooperating and working together or courting each other.
sentences.zh: 而且我们也真的很擅长合作、共同工作或互相追求。

sentences.en: So we can easily shift back and forth into different modes.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以轻松地在不同的模式之间来回切换。

sentences.en: I co-run a group called civilpolitics.org, where we're trying to promote civil political talk.
sentences.zh: 我共同运营着一个名为civilpolitics.org的组织，我们在那里努力推广温和理性的政治对话。

sentences.en: And here's what we say at the site.
sentences.zh: 以下是我们在网站上阐述的观点。

sentences.en: We say, civility, as we pursue it, is the ability to disagree productively with others, respecting their sincerity and decency.
sentences.zh: 我们说，我们所追求的文明素养，是指能够与他人进行富有成效的分歧探讨，同时尊重他们的真诚与正派。

sentences.en: And that's the key, is the sincerity and decency thing.
sentences.zh: 而这正是关键所在，也就是真诚与正派的问题。

sentences.en: When you're talking with people and you're arguing or disagreeing with them, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 当你与他人交谈、争论或持有不同意见时，这没有问题。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 这很好。

sentences.en: That's what politics is supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 这本该就是政治应有的样子。

sentences.en: But when what you're saying is aimed at discrediting their sincerity or decency, not rebutting their arguments, but saying, yeah,
sentences.zh: 但当你所说的话旨在抹黑他们的真诚或正派，而不是反驳他们的论点，而是说，没错，

sentences.en: you're just saying that because you're bribed by the Koch brothers or, you know, you're a fasciSt.
sentences.zh: 你这么说只是因为你被科赫兄弟收买了一直在拿钱，或者你知道的，你是个法西斯。

sentences.en: Those aren't real arguments.
sentences.zh: 那些并不是真正的论点。

sentences.en: Those are attempts to discredit the others.
sentences.zh: 那些都是试图抹黑他人的行为。

sentences.en: So that's the more adversarial, confrontational, zero-sum, or you might even say negative sum.
sentences.zh: 所以那是更具对抗性、冲突性、零和博弈的，甚至你可以说是负和博弈的。

sentences.en: The more I can hurt you, the better I am.
sentences.zh: 我能伤害你越多，对我自己就越好。

sentences.en: And that's what our politics has descended more into than it used to be.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的政治比过去更多堕落成的样子。

sentences.en: Well, it does seem like the divisiveness has reached a point where there's no turning back.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这种分裂似乎确实已经到了无法回头的地步。

sentences.en: I mean, you're saying that psychology and other social sciences can help us understand where we are, how we got here, and how to change.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是说心理学和其他社会科学可以帮助我们理解我们身处何地、我们是如何走到这一步的，以及如何做出改变。

sentences.en: Can you talk to us about that?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Well, sure, because there's no such thing as no turning back.
sentences.zh: 当然可以，因为根本没有“无法回头”这回事。

sentences.en: I mean, things were really, really bad.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，过去的情况曾经非常、非常糟糕。

sentences.en: I think the days of the Federalists and Anti-Federalists and, you know, the Founding Fathers, even Thomas Jefferson and others, were making up pen names.
sentences.zh: 我认为联邦党人和反联邦党人那个年代，你知道的，开国元勋们，甚至托马斯·杰斐逊和其他人，都在使用笔名。

sentences.en: And so they could attack each other anonymously, you know, like being trolls on the Internet almoSt.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以匿名攻击对方，你知道的，就像互联网上的喷子一样。

sentences.en: And the Civil War was, of course, much worse than things are today.
sentences.zh: 而内战当然比现在的情况要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: So things do go in cycles.
sentences.zh: 所以事情确实是有周期的。

sentences.en: Now things are at a low point.
sentences.zh: 现在事情正处于一个低谷期。

sentences.en: They've not been this bad, I think, since the late 19th century.
sentences.zh: 我认为，自19世纪末以来，情况还没有这么糟过。

sentences.en: So there is turning back, but it's going to be tough.
sentences.zh: 所以还是有办法回头的，但这将会很艰难。

sentences.en: There are a lot of trends that are pushing us this way now.
sentences.zh: 现在有很多趋势正在把我们往这个方向推。

sentences.en: What role does the popularity of social media, you know, Facebook, 24-hour news channels, constantly putting up pundits to say this and you say that, you know,
sentences.zh: 社交媒体的普及——你知道的，Facebook、24小时新闻频道，不断安排专家说这个说那个，你知道的——

sentences.en: what do they play in this divisiveness?
sentences.zh: 它们在产生这种分裂中扮演了什么角色？

sentences.en: Sam Abrams, who is a political scientist,
sentences.zh: 萨姆·亚伯拉罕斯，他是一位政治学家，

sentences.en: he and I wrote an essay in The Washington Post last year in which we described the 10 major trends that have made our politics so polarized and dysfunctional.
sentences.zh: 他和我去年在《华盛顿邮报》上合写了一篇文章，我们在文中描述了导致我们政治如此极化和失能的十大主要趋势。

sentences.en: The number one is the purification of the parties.
sentences.zh: 排在第一位的是政党的纯洁化。

sentences.en: So we didn't used to have a clear conservative party and a clear progressive party.
sentences.zh: 所以过去我们并没有一个清晰的保守派政党和一个清晰的进步派政党。

sentences.en: There was a left and right wing of both parties up until really until the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪70年代真正到来之前，两个政党内部都既有左翼也有右翼。

sentences.en: But once after President Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act and that made the conservative Democrats leave, in the South especially, leave the Democratic Party,
sentences.zh: 但在约翰逊总统签署《民权法案》之后，这使得保守派民主党人离开，特别是在南部，离开了民主党，

sentences.en: join the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 加入了共和党。

sentences.en: In 1964, that's right.
So that starts these tectonic plates shifting, which gives us a purified liberal progressive party and a purified conservative party.
sentences.zh: 所以这引发了这些板块的移动，从而给我们带来了一个纯洁的自由进步派政党和一个纯洁的保守派政党。

sentences.en: And so that really begins to take shape in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 这在20世纪80年代开始真正成形。

sentences.en: And by the 90s, it's complete.
sentences.zh: 到了90年代，这就彻底完成了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So you asked me about social media.
sentences.zh: 所以你问我关于社交媒体的事。

sentences.en: Well, this is the back story to it.
sentences.zh: 这就是这一切的背景故事。

sentences.en: Once you have these purified parties, and that happens at the same time as this media revolution where you got cable TV and then the Internet,
sentences.zh: 一旦你有了这些纯洁化的政党，而这又与媒体革命同时发生，你当时有了有线电视，然后是互联网，

sentences.en: so that now the media that people consume is all confirmatory.
sentences.zh: 以至于现在人们消费的媒体全都是相互印证的。

sentences.en: Everybody can tune into things that support their worldview.
sentences.zh: 每个人都可以收听那些支持他们世界观的内容。

sentences.en: So those two trends interact to give us this perfect storm where everyone is now totally convinced, not just that they're right,
sentences.zh: 因此，这两种趋势相互作用，造就了这场完美的风暴，现在每个人都完全确信，不仅他们自己是正确的，

sentences.en: but that the other side is racist or fascist or funded by the Kochs or PC, whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 而且另一方是种族主义者、法西斯主义者、由科赫家族资助的或者政治正确的，无论是什么。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's real bad.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，情况真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: I was talking with somebody at the APA convention about this the other day, and we kind of worked up the metaphor.
sentences.zh: 前几天我在APA（美国心理学协会）大会上跟某人谈起过这个，我们琢磨出了一个隐喻。

sentences.en: It's like if you go back – social media, to me, is like this technology that we're just not – we're not adapted for yet.
sentences.zh: 这就好比你回溯——对我而言，社交媒体就像是一项我们根本还没准备好、还没适应的技术。

sentences.en: We're not used to yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还不习惯它。

sentences.en: So it's like imagine if you go back 50,000 years, and humans are just leaving Africa, and we have spear technology.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比想象一下，如果你回到5万年前，人类刚刚离开非洲，我们拥有了长矛技术。

sentences.en: We've had spears for about a half million years.
sentences.zh: 我们使用长矛大约有五十万年了。

sentences.en: We kind of know how to kill each other with spears, but we also know how to get along when there's all these spears around.
sentences.zh: 我们多少知道如何用长矛杀死彼此，但我们也知道在周围全都是长矛的时候该如何相处。

sentences.en: So we've been living with spears for half a million years.
sentences.zh: 所以我们和长矛一起生活了五十万年。

sentences.en: But suddenly some malevolent other species from another planet drops loaded handguns all over the world so that you get this – the spear technology people,
sentences.zh: 但突然之间，来自另一个星球的某个心怀恶意的其他物种在全世界到处投放装好子弹的手枪，于是你得到了这个——习惯了长矛技术的人们，

sentences.en: and they suddenly – everybody's got loaded handguns.
sentences.zh: 他们突然——每个人都拥有了装好子弹的手枪。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 就像什么？

sentences.en: What are these things?
sentences.zh: 这些东西是什么？

sentences.en: You pull the trigger.
sentences.zh: 你扣动扳机。

sentences.en: The other guy's dead.
sentences.zh: 另一个人就死了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: This is great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: There'd be a lot of killing.
sentences.zh: 那将会发生大量的杀戮。

sentences.en: Eventually we presume they'd work out norms for how to live with handguns, but it would take a while.
sentences.zh: 最终我们猜测他们会摸索出如何与手枪共存的规范，但这需要一段时间。

sentences.en: That's where we are with social media.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们对待社交媒体的现状。

sentences.en: We all really care about reputations, and we suddenly have this technology that allows us to slander anyone else instantly, to draw a mob.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都非常在意声誉，而我们突然拥有了这样一项技术，它允许我们瞬间诽谤任何人，煽动暴民。

sentences.en: So what's happened is people are really, really afraid.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的事情是，人们真的、真的很害怕。

sentences.en: I see this on college campuses.
sentences.zh: 我在大学校园里看到了这一点。

sentences.en: People are so afraid to stand up, stand out, say anything unless it's with the mob.
sentences.zh: 人们太害怕站出来、崭露头角、说任何话了，除非是跟暴民站在同一边。

sentences.en: If the mob is on their side, then they are so vocal and self-righteous.
sentences.zh: 如果暴民站在他们这一边，那么他们就会变得非常吵闹且自以为是。

sentences.en: But what I'm finding is that even moderists or centrist, people who are not political, are afraid to speak up and challenge the left because they'll get crucified.
sentences.zh: 但我发现的是，即使是温和派或中间派，那些不怎么关心政治的人，也害怕发声并挑战左翼，因为他们会被群起而攻之。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: An Associated Press poll last year found that Republican voters want their congressional leaders to stick to conservative principles while Democrats favor compromise.
sentences.zh: 美联社去年的一项民意调查发现，共和党选民希望他们的国会领袖坚持保守派原则，而民主党人则赞成妥协。

sentences.en: And there are many more differences between the two parties.
sentences.zh: 两党之间还有更多差异。

sentences.en: Your expertise is in moral psychology, which is kind of a broad term encompassing ethics, psychology, and philosophy.
sentences.zh: 你的专业领域是道德心理学，这是一个包含伦理学、心理学和哲学的广泛术语。

sentences.en: Can you talk about how psychology can help us explain these differences?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈心理学如何帮助我们解释这些差异吗？

sentences.en: Oh, sure.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: It's been a major area of research for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 对于很多人来说，这一直是主要的科研领域。

sentences.en: There are a lot of—well, if you want to understand left-right differences, some of it is true asymmetries.
sentences.zh: 有很多——嗯，如果你想理解左右翼的差异，其中一些确实是不对称性。

sentences.en: That is, people on the left psychologically are different from people on the right.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在心理上，左翼人士与右翼人士是不同的。

sentences.en: And the most consistent differences are that people on the left are higher on openness to experience, they enjoy variety and diversity,
sentences.zh: 最一致的差异在于，左翼人士在对新体验的开放性上得分更高，他们喜欢变化和多样性，

sentences.en: and then also they're a little lower on conscientiousness.
sentences.zh: 然后他们在尽责性上稍微低一点。

sentences.en: So you put this all together, and what you get is people on the left are more interested in immigration, diversity, variety.
sentences.zh: 所以你把这些综合起来，你就会发现左翼人士对移民、多样性、变化更感兴趣。

sentences.en: The research by Sam Gosling at UT Austin shows that if you look at the dorm rooms of people—he did this study at Berkeley—you go into people's dorm rooms when they're not there.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校萨姆·戈斯林的研究所表明，如果你看看人们的宿舍房间——他在伯克利做过这项研究——当人们不在的时候，你走进他们的宿舍房间。

sentences.en: They give you permission to go in.
sentences.zh: 他们会允许你进去。

sentences.en: You just take photographs.
sentences.zh: 你只需要拍照片。

sentences.en: You code things.
sentences.zh: 你对物品进行编码分类。

sentences.en: And then you show those to other students to just rate, do you think this person is liberal or conservative?
sentences.zh: 然后你把这些展示给其他学生让他们来评判，你认为这个人是自由派还是保守派？

sentences.en: People can tell.
sentences.zh: 人们能够分辨出来。

sentences.en: Liberals are less organized.
sentences.zh: 自由派的组织性较差。

sentences.en: They have more high style.
sentences.zh: 他们更有时尚感。

sentences.en: They have fewer calendars.
sentences.zh: 他们的日历更少。

sentences.en: Conservatives are more organized, responsible.
sentences.zh: 保守派更有组织性、更负责任。

sentences.en: Their music and books are from a narrower range.
sentences.zh: 他们的音乐和书籍来自较窄的范围。

sentences.en: So there are psychological differences.
sentences.zh: 所以确实存在心理学上的差异。

sentences.en: Neither one is good or bad, but it does help explain why they differ on issues of immigration, nationalism, patriotism, all those sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 这两者无所谓好坏，但它确实有助于解释为什么他们在移民、民族主义、爱国主义等所有这些问题上存在分歧。

sentences.en: So you start with those, and that means that people who are born with a certain personality, as they grow up, they're going to find right-wing or left-wing ideas more congenial.
sentences.zh: 所以你从这些开始，这意味着那些生来带有某种人格的人，在他们长大后，会发现右翼或左翼的思想更加契合他们的心意。

sentences.en: Our genes don't predestine us to be on one side, but they make one side or the other more likely.
sentences.zh: 我们的基因并没有预先注定我们要站在哪一边，但它们使得某一边或另一边更有可能发生。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of interesting research on personality and politics.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多关于人格与政治的有趣研究。

sentences.en: Then the next thing you have to bring in is group dynamics.
sentences.zh: 接下来你必须引入的是群体动力学。

sentences.en: So you get these two groups fighting it out, and your question was about issues of compromise.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到这两个群体在激烈争斗，而你的问题是关于妥协的问题。

sentences.en: Well, yes, it's true that right now the word compromise is a dirty word for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，的确现在对共和党人来说“妥协”这个词是一个肮脏的词。

sentences.en: And there was some funny episodes five years ago, a lot of us remember, when I forget which journalist was trying to get John Boehner to say the word compromise.
sentences.zh: 五年前有一些有趣的插曲，我们很多人都还记得，当时我忘了是哪个记者试图让约翰·博纳说出“妥协”这个词。

sentences.en: And he wouldn't say it because he knows that if he in any way endorsed compromise, his people would consider him a traitor.
sentences.zh: 而他就是不肯说，因为他知道，如果他以任何方式支持妥协，他的人民就会认为他是叛徒。

sentences.en: So is it that the right is more closed-minded and against compromise?
sentences.zh: 那么，是不是右翼思想更封闭、更反对妥协？

sentences.en: It depends a lot on which side feels more embattled, which side feels it's being crushed, which side is more self-righteous.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上取决于哪一方感觉自己更受围困、哪一方觉得自己正在被压垮、哪一方更加自以为是。

sentences.en: And so that can shift.
sentences.zh: 所以这是可以改变的。

sentences.en: That can go back and forth.
sentences.zh: 这是可以来回转变的。

sentences.en: There is also the interesting difference that in studies of, like, trolley dilemmas of, you know, would you push a man off a bridge, one man, to save the lives of five,
sentences.zh: 还有一个有趣的差异，在诸如电车难题之类的研究中——你知道的，你会不会把一个人推下桥，一个人，来拯救五个人的生命，

sentences.en: there's some research showing that conservatives are more deontological.
sentences.zh: 有一些研究表明，保守派更具道义论倾向。

sentences.en: That means they go more with absolute rules and principles, like, no, you don't kill someone.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们更遵循绝对的规则和原则，比如，不，你不能杀人。

sentences.en: You don't push someone off a bridge.
sentences.zh: 你不能把人推下桥。

sentences.en: So it is possible that people on the right are more principled in the sense of these are the rules.
sentences.zh: 所以右翼人士在“这些就是规则”这种意义上可能更讲原则。

sentences.en: You don't break them, whereas people on the left are more like, well, you know, you've got to look at the outcomes, do all these tradeoffs.
sentences.zh: 你不能打破它们，而左翼人士则更倾向于，好吧，你知道的，你必须看结果，权衡所有这些利弊。

sentences.en: So in that case, I don't know for sure whether it's truly that the right is more opposed to compromise.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我无法确定右翼是否真的更加反对妥协。

sentences.en: You have to look at all these different factors.
sentences.zh: 你必须审视所有这些不同的因素。

sentences.en: So how can we use psychology to reduce the intensity of these conflicts?
sentences.zh: 那么我们如何利用心理学来降低这些冲突的烈度呢？

sentences.en: I mean, like you say, we're always going to have them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就像你说的，我们总是会面临这些冲突。

sentences.en: There's some differences and conflict between, but how do we reduce the intensity of it?
sentences.zh: 之间总会有一些分歧和冲突，但我们如何降低它的烈度呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, this is where social psychology can be so helpful.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，这就是社会心理学可以发挥巨大作用的地方。

sentences.en: Because one of the great psychological aphorisms or quotations, there's a Bedouin proverb that says,
sentences.zh: 因为最伟大的心理学格言或语录之一，有一句贝都因人的谚语说，

sentences.en: me against my brother, me and my brother against our cousin, and me, my brother and cousin against the stranger.
sentences.zh: 我对抗我的兄弟，我和我兄弟对抗我们的堂兄弟，而我和我兄弟以及堂兄弟一起对抗外人。

sentences.en: So we're tribal, we're tribal creatures.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是部落属性的，我们是部落生物。

sentences.en: And it used to be in American politics that they would say, politics ends at the water's edge.
sentences.zh: 过去在美国政治中，他们会说，政治止于水边。

sentences.en: Sure, we can fight it out, you know, Democrat, Republican, but as soon as there's a foreign policy issue, we stop that and we're united.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们可以争吵，你知道的，民主党人，共和党人，但一旦出现外交政策问题，我们就会停止争吵并团结一致。

sentences.en: And that was the case when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候就是这样。

sentences.en: You heard that a lot.
sentences.zh: 你经常听到这种说法。

sentences.en: But beginning in the 90s, that stopped being the case.
sentences.zh: 但从90年代开始，情况就不再是这样了。

sentences.en: Now, it's basically me and my brother against our cousin, and we don't care what else is happening.
sentences.zh: 现在，基本上就是我和我兄弟去对抗我们的堂兄弟，至于其他发生的事我们根本不在乎。

sentences.en: We just hate the cousin, and no matter who we're being attacked by, we're going to focus on fighting the cousin.
sentences.zh: 我们只是痛恨那个表亲，不管我们受到谁的攻击，我们都要集中精力对付那个表亲。

sentences.en: So our partisanship is kind of stuck.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的党派性有点陷入了僵局。

sentences.en: But there's a lot you can do to move things around, because in addition to being tribal, humans are also really cooperative and we're really good at trade.
sentences.zh: 但你可以做很多事情来扭转局面，因为除了具有部落倾向外，人类也非常具有合作精神，而且我们非常擅长贸易。

sentences.en: You know, our ancestors were really good at leaving their tribe and going out and finding other groups to exchange with.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们的祖先非常擅长离开自己的部落，出去寻找其他群体进行交流。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of hope.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面有很大的希望。

sentences.en: One of the most consistent findings in social psychology is that when you give groups a superordinate threat or goal, some project to work on together,
sentences.zh: 社会心理学中最一致的发现之一是，当你给各个群体一个共同的威胁或目标，也就是某种需要共同完成的项目时，

sentences.en: they tend to drop the tribalism and work together.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会抛弃部落主义，并肩作战。

sentences.en: I was very fortunate to be involved with a group.
sentences.zh: 我非常有幸能参与其中一个小组。

sentences.en: I was able to moderate a group of poverty experts, some of the top experts on the right and left on poverty.
sentences.zh: 我能够主持一个由贫困问题专家组成的小组，其中包括左右翼的一些顶尖贫困问题专家。

sentences.en: And in our first few meetings, we worked for about a year in 2015, we worked for a year together.
sentences.zh: 在我们最初的几次会议中，我们在2015年一起工作了大约一年，我们一起工作了一年。

sentences.en: And our first few meetings, it was really clear there was the left team and the right team.
sentences.zh: 在我们最初的几次会议上，很明显存在左翼团队和右翼团队。

sentences.en: And the left team was really focused on economic causes of poverty and structural problems and racism.
sentences.zh: 左翼团队真正关注的是贫困的经济根源、结构性问题以及种族主义。

sentences.en: And the right was really focused on family breakdown and the need for order and discipline and self-control and delay of gratification.
sentences.zh: 而右翼则真正关注家庭解体，以及对秩序、纪律、自我控制和延迟满足的需求。

sentences.en: And, you know, and at first it was really clear, well, you know, actually, both sides are actually right.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，起初很明显，嗯，你知道的，实际上，双方其实都是对的。

sentences.en: And we just have to figure out a way that they can, we can incorporate all of their insights into the final report.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要想出一个办法，让他们能够，我们可以把他们所有的见解都纳入到最终报告中。

sentences.en: And what was most thrilling was that by the end of this year-long process, there wasn't a right team or a left team anymore.
sentences.zh: 最让人兴奋的是，到这一年进程结束时，不再有什么右翼团队或左翼团队了。

sentences.en: And one of our last meetings, I gave the groups the option of caucusing separately because, you know, we had these final recommendations.
sentences.zh: 在我们最后的一次会议上，我给小组成员提供了分开开会的选项，因为，你知道的，我们有这些最终建议。

sentences.en: And, okay, do you guys need to talk separately to be sure you endorse these?
sentences.zh: 然后，好吧，你们需要分开谈谈以确保你们支持这些建议吗？

sentences.en: And they all said, no, no, we don't, we don't, no, you know, let's talk about it all together.
sentences.zh: 他们都说，不，不，我们不需要，我们不需要，不，你知道的，我们一起谈谈吧。

sentences.en: They really had a sense of, we've been working on this thing for a year.
sentences.zh: 他们真的有一种感觉，我们已经为这件事努力了一年。

sentences.en: We've, we've come so far.
sentences.zh: 我们，我们已经走了这么远。

sentences.en: We have a great set of recommendations.
sentences.zh: 我们有一套很棒的建议。

sentences.en: So it can take some time, but if you foster relationships and a sense of common or shared group identity with a common goal or project, you can break down the tribalism.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能需要一些时间，但如果你培养人际关系以及围绕共同目标或项目的共同或共享的群体认同感，你就能打破部落主义。

sentences.en: Switching gears a little bit to the field of psychology, what have you learned about the political leanings of psychologists themselves?
sentences.zh: 话题稍微转向心理学领域，关于心理学家自身的政治倾向，你了解到了什么？

sentences.en: And how does that affect the field's viewpoint on politically controversial topics?
sentences.zh: 这又如何影响该领域对政治争议话题的看法？

sentences.en: Oh, my.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Well, so, you know, what's been happening to our country since the 90s or so is that the,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道的，自20世纪90年代左右以来，我们的国家一直在发生的事情是，

sentences.en: it's almost like a gigantic electromagnet with a positive pole and a negative pole pulling us apart.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个带有正极和负极的巨大电磁铁，把我们拉开。

sentences.en: And we're seeing whole, you know, we're seeing religious denominations splitting over this into the, you know, the more left-wing Episcopalians and the right-wing Episcopalians.
sentences.zh: 我们看到整个，你知道的，我们看到宗教教派因此分裂为，你知道的，更偏左的圣公会教徒和右翼的圣公会教徒。

sentences.en: And that's been happening in universities.
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直在大学里发生。

sentences.en: Universities have leaned left for more than 100 years.
sentences.zh: 大学向左倾斜已经有100多年了。

sentences.en: And that's not really a problem in my view.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这并不是什么真正的问题。

sentences.en: I don't, we don't have to have 50-50 parity and everything.
sentences.zh: 我并不觉得，我们没必要在每件事上都保持50对50的对等。

sentences.en: What we must have in the science is we must have the certainty that ideas will be critiqued.
sentences.zh: 我们在科学中必须做到的是，我们必须确信各种观点会受到批判。

sentences.en: So if somebody says something that's, you know, very sort of left, we don't, pleases the left, it's got to be the case that someone will stand up and say, well, wait a second,
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人说了某种，你知道的，非常偏左的话，我们不会，迎合了左翼，那必须得有人站出来说，嗯，等一下，

sentences.en: you're making this assumption.
sentences.zh: 你是在做这个假设。

sentences.en: You know, somebody has to be there to say that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，必须得有人在那里说出这句话。

sentences.en: And so until the 90s, there were some people around who were not on the left.
sentences.zh: 所以在90年代之前，周围总有一些不属于左翼的人。

sentences.en: But what's happened in psychology and in the social sciences more broadly, and it happened especially in the humanities, is they shifted from being on the left or leaning left,
sentences.zh: 但心理学以及更广泛的社会科学中发生的事情，尤其是人文科学中发生的事情是，他们从左翼或偏向左翼，

sentences.en: two or three to one, to leaning left, 10 to one, 20 to one, on some measures, 30 or 40 to one, which means that you will never find someone who's not on the left.
sentences.zh: 比例从三比一或二比一，变成了偏向左翼十比一、二十比一，在某些指标上甚至达到三十或四十比一，这意味着你永远找不到一个不属于左翼的人。

sentences.en: Or rather, there are a few, but they don't dare speak up.
sentences.zh: 或者更确切地说，有一些人，但他们不敢发声。

sentences.en: Even the centrists, what I find is that even in surveys, even people who say, I'm not on the right, I'm in the middle, you know,
sentences.zh: 甚至连中间派也是如此，我发现即使在调查中，甚至那些说“我不是右翼，我在中间”的人，你知道的，

sentences.en: are you willing to speak up and challenge things when, if they're politically controversial?
sentences.zh: 当事情具有政治争议时，你愿意大声说出来并提出质疑吗？

sentences.en: No, no, it's just too dangerous.
sentences.zh: 不，不，这太危险了。

sentences.en: So the social sciences, I think, are breaking down, not entirely, but on politicized topics.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为社会科学正在崩溃，并非完全崩溃，但在政治化的话题上确实如此。

sentences.en: If we're talking about race, gender, immigration, inequality, whatever the favorite topics are, I think the research coming out is just not, it's not, well,
sentences.zh: 如果我们谈论种族、性别、移民、不平等，无论哪些是热门话题，我认为产出的研究就是不行，它不行，嗯，

sentences.en: individual research projects can be very good, but the overall output is really tilted, and a lot of ideas are there because they're politically pleasing,
sentences.zh: 个别的研究项目可能非常好，但整体产出严重倾斜，很多观点的存在是因为它们在政治上讨喜，

sentences.en: not because they're empirically supported.
sentences.zh: 而不是因为它们有经验证据的支持。

sentences.en: It's a huge problem, and that's why I started a group with some friends of mine called heterodoxacademy.org.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的问题，这就是为什么我和几个朋友创办了一个名为 heterodoxacademy.org 的组织。

sentences.en: I urge listeners to go check it out.
sentences.zh: 我敦促听众去看看。

sentences.en: We make the case that the academy needs more viewpoint diversity.
sentences.zh: 我们提出，学术界需要更多的观点多样性。

sentences.en: Diversity is a good thing, but the most important kind of diversity is viewpoint diversity.
sentences.zh: 多样性是一件好事，但最要紧的多样性是观点多样性。

sentences.en: You have to have people who actually think differently.
sentences.zh: 你必须拥有那些真正有不同思考方式的人。

sentences.en: Just to have people who are a different race or sex doesn't help your thinking, unless they think differently.
sentences.zh: 仅仅拥有不同种族或性别的人对你的思考并没有帮助，除非他们的思考方式不同。

sentences.en: And we've been so focused on those demographic diversity things that it's actually made the viewpoint diversity issue even harder,
sentences.zh: 我们一直太专注于这些人口统计学上的多样性问题，以至于实际上让观点多样性问题变得更加困难，

sentences.en: because when everyone's focused on race and gender diversity, then they're almost all on the left, and they see conservatives as the enemy, as they're racist and sexiSt.
sentences.zh: 因为当每个人都专注于种族和性别多样性时，他们几乎全都在左翼，并且将保守派视为敌人，认为他们是种族主义者和性别歧视者。

sentences.en: We don't want them here.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望他们在这里。

sentences.en: And this is what's happened in psychology as in the other social sciences.
sentences.zh: 这就是心理学和其他社会科学中发生的事情。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Haidt, thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 海特博士，非常感谢您做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: I appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 我很感激您抽出时间。

sentences.en: It's been great.
sentences.zh: 非常棒。

sentences.en: My pleasure, Audrey.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸，奥黛丽。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: If you would like more information on the topics we discussed, or if you would like to hear more episodes, please go to our website at speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您想了解有关我们讨论话题的更多信息，或者想收听更多单集，请访问我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org。

sentences.en: With the American Psychological Association's Speaking of Psychology, I'm Audrey Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 这里是美国心理学会的《心理学话语》，我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。
